newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-WAQAR BATS GLAMORGAN TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WAQAR BATS GLAMORGAN TO VICTORY.

text.p: Pakistan fast bowler Waqar Younis clinched a one-wicket NatWest Trophy quarter-final win for Glamorgan over Yorkshire on Tuesday -- but with the bat and not the ball.
There seemed no hope for Glamorgan when they slumped from 140 for two to 209 for nine chasing Yorkshire's 236 for eight.
Waqar finished with 34 not out after England paceman Darren Gough had looked to have set up Yorkshire for their third successive NatWest semifinal by taking four for 36.
But Waqar and last man Dean Cosker survived everything the Yorkshire bowlers sent down to finally win with six balls remaining.

Yorkshire's total was built around a high-class 105 from Australian Darren Lehmann, who held his side together after Cosker and spinner Robert Croft had pegged them to 94 for four at the halfway mark of 30 overs.
Late replacement Rajesh Rao set a county record as he hammered 158 to steer outsiders Sussex into the semifinals with a five-wicket win over Derbyshire.

The 22-year-old batsman, who has made only five first-class appearances, hit 18 boundaries in his 165-ball innings as Sussex made 329 for five with four balls to spare after chasing a formidable 327 for eight.

Rao was drafted into the Sussex line-up after Neil Lenham failed to prove his fitness following a heel injury. He beat the previous highest individual one-day score of 141 by Gehan Mendis against Warwickshire 17 years ago.
Derbyshire's formidable total was built around an unbeaten 129 by Chris Adams who hit hit eight fours and a six.
England vice-captain Nasser Hussain dropped Essex into a big hole and then dug them out of it as his side overcame Nottinghamshire by three wickets at Trent Bridge.
He dropped catches off opener Tim Robinson once and century-maker Paul Johnson twice, and the duo between them went on to score an additional 124 runs after their let-offs.
It left Essex facing an imposing 289 for victory, but Hussain made up for his fielding nightmare by top-scoring with an unbeaten 89 as his side won with 10 balls to spare.
Warwickshire completed the semifinal line-up with a 28-run victory in which Mark Ramprakash of Middlesex may have boosted his England prospects despite ending up on the losing side at Lord's.
Ramprakash made 98 but it was not enough to help the home side overhaul Warwickshire's 286 for six in which David Hemp's 112 earned him the man of the match award.

The writing was on the wall for Middlesex when they needed 91 with 10 overs left and another England contender, left-arm spinner Ashley Giles, ended any hope of a dramatic recovery by claiming three wickets in a fine spell.
